CI phases

scripts/ci.mjs

In call order, read out of main(). A fast phase also runs on --fast and in the pre-push hook; the rest only on a full run.

01
hygienefast

Everything here is about the difference between THIS working copy and a fresh clone.

02
structurefast

The architecture rules, run over this repo's own apps and packages with the same engine `fli check` gives a client app.

03
registersfast

The three registers, graded against the rules they state about themselves.

04
snapshotsfast

A snapshot is a generated artefact committed beside its source, so a change nothing else in the repo can see arrives as a diff: the access rules enforced below the API, the DDL every hand-written statement binds to, the JSON Schema three packages validate…

05
accessfast

What did this branch do to who may do what.

06
coveragefast

Skipped is not passed. The aggregate `--filter '*'` walks straight past a package with no `test` script and prints nothing at all about it.

07
registryfast

Scaffolds an app, packs the working tree into it, installs and builds it.

08
advisoriesfast

Dependency posture, decided the way everything else here is decided: a phase, not a bot (`IDEAS/tooling-decisions.md` 5).

09
scaffoldfast
10
typecheckfast

Two halves: the direction of the ratchet (a git question) and the count itself (each package's own script already answers that, and exits 1 above its ceiling).

11
deployfull run

`fli new` → `fli make:deploy` → `fli deploy:local`: does the deploy pipeline containerise a real app? ~30s and it needs a Docker daemon, so it sits in the full tier rather than the pre-push one.

12
testsfull run

Sequential on purpose: several suites bind ports and start real servers, and interleaved output from four different runners is unreadable when one fails.

litestone7repo6sierra5basecamp4cli4litestone · sierra4css2example2example · basecamp2basecamp · outpost1cli · basecamp1cli · ci1cli · css1cli · litestone1conduit1email-kit1example · junction1example · litestone1junction1junction — A multipart boundary is case-sensitive and parseBody lowercased it, so no browser had ever uploaded a file to a Junction app. The header was lowercased whole — correct for the media type, which is case-insensitive — and the boundary was then read out of that lowercased copy. A media type's PARAMETERS are not case-insensitive, and RFC 2046 §5.1.1 says so about this parameter by name. Chrome and Safari send ----WebKitFormBoundary…; lowercased, it matches nothing in the body, so no part is found, data is {} and ctx.data is falsy — and the request answers Request body is required about a request that plainly has one. Every probe of this path passed, which is why it survived: curl, Bun's own new Request({ body: form }) and undici all generate lowercase-hex boundaries, and junction's one existing multipart test asserted the parsed body's TYPE and never its contents. It was found by putting a real file input in a real browser, and it could not have been found any other way1junction · litestone1litestone — findUnique ran no plugin read hook and logged no read, so get(id) — the most common read an app makes — answered a different shape from every other read. findFirst, findMany and findManyAndCount each end with plugins.afterRead(...) and emitLogs('read', …); findUnique had neither, on either of its two paths, while calling beforeRead — which is what made the gap look like plugin support rather than half of it. Consequences, both silent: ExternalRefPlugin resolves a stored file reference into a public URL in onAfterRead, so a File column came back as raw {"key":…,"provider":…} from get(id) and as a URL from the same column read by find — an <img src> that works in a list and is broken on the detail screen beside it, and an edit form handed the storage handle instead of the photograph. And a @@log model recorded reads through every path but this one. The ultra-fast path skips beforeRead too, which is correct rather than a hole: canFastFindUnique requires there to be no plugins at all — but it can be taken on a table that declares @@log, so the read entry was missing there as well. Found while wiring FJS-4091litestone · cli1litestone · junction1litestone · junction · sierra · toolbelt1mesa1mesa · cli1sierra — vite dev on a static surface called the BUILD-TIME loader in the browser, so the storefront rendered empty and the terminal filled with warnings about the migration engine. A render: static route's load() runs in Node at build time and is where an app reads its own database; the client route table kept its import anyway, and the comment beside the omission said so out loud — dev is untouched, vite dev on a static target IS a client-routed app and calls load() in the browser, so the loaders have to be there. True of a client-routed page and false of a prerendered one. What happened instead: the router imported the companion, called it, and got Module "fs" has been externalized for browser compatibility — caught, downgraded to a console.warn, and rendered as a page with nothing on it, which is indistinguishable from a query that returned no rows. On the way there Vite followed the same import into the browser graph and reported eight un-analyzable dynamic imports from litestone's migration runner, junction's config loader, its service autoloader and its database storage — noise that reads as a broken install and is one step from the published-directory hazard the BUILD's omission already closed. FJS-556 conduit Every outbound body is JSON.stringifyd unconditionally, so conduit cannot speak to a form-encoded API at all 2026-08-27 transports/http.ts sets rawBody = serialise(req.body) and serialise is JSON.stringify with no way past it. Content-Type IS overridable — ...req.headers is spread after the application/json default — so a caller can say application/x-www-form-urlencoded and have the bytes still be JSON, which is the worst shape: the request looks configured and the provider reads {"amount":500} where it expects amount=500. Passing a pre-encoded string does not help either, since JSON.stringify('amount=500') is "amount=500" with the quotes. Stripe, PayPal, Twilio and every OAuth token endpoint are form-encoded, so this is not one vendor being unusual. The fix belongs in the transport and nowhere else, because rawBody is the same string handed to buildAuthHeaders — an encoder living in a caller or a connector would sign bytes the transport did not send (FJS-D153). Shape: an encoding: 'json' \

FJS-456 sierra A prerendered site's sitemap.xml lists no dynamic page, so a storefront's sitemap omits every product 2026-08-23 generateSitemap is handed routeTable.indexed, which is filtered to exclude dynamic routes — correct for an SPA, where /products/:slug/ is not a URL — and the static build then emits one file per getStaticPaths() entry and tells the sitemap nothing about them. Measured on example/site: 15 pages emitted, sitemap.xml (3 URLs) — /, /404/, /catalog/ — so the twelve pages the site exists to publish are the twelve it does not list. (/404/ being IN it is a second, smaller wrong: a not-found page is the one page that should never be indexed.) The build already has the answer — prerenderRoutes returns written, one relative path per emitted page — so the shape of the fix is to merge those in. What stops it being a two-line change is the FILTER: indexed also drops status: draft and robots: noindex, and those are declared on the ROUTE, so a dynamic route marked noindex must not have its twelve pages appear just because they were emitted. That needs the emitted paths to carry their route id, which written does not. Related and not the same: a static build also emits the SPA entry bundle, which no prerendered page links — dist/index.html is overwritten by the prerendered home page — so a static target ships a client bundle nothing loads. Whether that should be emitted at all is the same question asked about a different artefact

Which file answers which question

each one holds a single kind of statement

Quoted from each file's own opening claim. When you cannot find something, the question to ask is what kind of statement it is.

ARCHITECT.md

The mental model and its vocabulary.

CLAUDE.md

Bun-workspace monorepo: a schema-seeded fullstack framework.

DECISIONS.md

Dated rulings by the project owner.

HANDOFF.md

The expression has one owner and it must stay that way.

ISSUES_ARCHIVE.md

Closed items, moved out of ISSUES.md so the register stays the list of what is live.

ISSUES.md

The register of everything open in this repo.

PHILOSOPHY.md

Most of a web application is restatement — the same fact, written five times in five dialects: an ORM schema, a validation library, a TypeScript…

PROS_AND_CONS.md

Written 2026-08-03.

README.md

A full-stack JavaScript framework built on Bun.
